title: Mixed-size sequence padding can cause a heap buffer overflow
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner (model not specified for this finding)
summary: Padding an image to a requested size that was larger in one dimension and smaller in another could cause heap buffer overflow during sequence encoding. The path is reachable when x264/x265 encoders process later frames with different sizes from the first frame.
ai_role: The item-level libheif advisory explicitly attributes discovery to Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-QL0PMTMT. The release notes independently state that all listed security issues were found by the scanner. The Anthropic program sources establish model-based scanning, but no per-case model is identified.
classification_note: The primary advisory establishes a publicly disclosed security finding and direct Anthropic OSS Scanner attribution. No CVE had been assigned in the libheif release notes at the checked time; the distinct GHSA is used. No exploitation or zero-day status is asserted.
remediation_note: Padding now rejects dimensions below the image or its planes and validates all planes before changes; sequence encoders reject mixed-size frames. Fixed in libheif 1.23.7. This concerns encoding workflows, not ordinary file decoding. The libheif v1.23.7 security release is dated 2026-10-26; deployed patch status is not checked.

impacts.conditions: A crafted mixed-size image sequence can cause a heap buffer overflow and crash when an application accepts the sequence and re-encodes it using the affected encoder. No code execution is demonstrated.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited description.
